body:
**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

so for testing, do you know if Oracle supports CTE for UPDATE and DELETE also?   most of the work here is building out the test suite to start exercising so-called "Backend" cte expressions against different databases.

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* removed labels: **low priority**

**James Frick wrote:**

Update syntax is the same:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40341125/cte-and-table-update-in-oracle

Delete syntax is similar, though the only way I could get a working example is with an ANY or EXISTS.
https://www.w3resource.com/sql/delete-statement/delete-with-subqueries.php
```
delete from foo
where col_a = any(
with cte1 as (select col_a from foo)
select distinct col_a from cte1
)
```
That would delete all rows successfully. Tested in Oracle 12c.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK I may need to break out the testing requirements markers a bit for that....this is all on my end

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK that UPDATE syntax is not the full blown CTE UPDATE postgresql supports, as that requires UPDATE..FROM.    So I need to test that separately

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK....in order to move forward we're going to get the test support in, which is also #4230, and get INSERT ...WITH..SELECT working.  the embedding of the WITH inside the subquery is a bigger issue that I'm going to leave out for now (doesn't work like that, CTE always goes to the top).

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

render WITH clause after INSERT for INSERT..SELECT on Oracle, MySQL

Fixed INSERT FROM SELECT with CTEs for the Oracle and MySQL dialects, where
the CTE was being placed above the entire statement as is typical with
other databases, however Oracle and MariaDB 10.2 wants the CTE underneath
the "INSERT" segment. Note that the Oracle and MySQL dialects don't yet
work when a CTE is applied to a subquery inside of an UPDATE or DELETE
statement, as the CTE is still applied to the top rather than inside the
subquery.

Also adds test suite support CTEs against backends.

Fixes: #4275

issue.title: question: malformed insert statement when calling `create_table` with Postgres backend
issue.body:
### What happened?

When trying to create tables form expressions which compile to SQL containing a CTE clause, the insert statements render with a syntax error - placing the `insert into ...` in the middle of the statement, rather the beginning.

E.g. the following code

```python
ibis_connection = ibis.postgres.connect(...)
X = ibis_connection.table('X')
X.join(X.mutate(a=X['id'] % 1))
X = X.join(X.mutate(a=X['id'] + 1), ['id'])
ibis.show_sql(X)

> WITH t0 AS (
>   SELECT
>     t1.id AS id,
>     t1.id + 1 AS a
>   FROM dg_test AS t1
> )
> SELECT
>   t1.id,
>   t0.a
> FROM dg_test AS t1
> JOIN t0
>   ON t1.id = t0.id
```

When I call `ibis_connection.create_table('test', X)`, `sqlalchemy` throws `SyntaxError: syntax error at or near "INSERT"` due the following insert statement (note that `insert into` should _begin_ the statement)

```sql
WITH t0 AS 
(SELECT t1.id AS id, t1.id + %(param_1)s AS a 
FROM dg_test AS t1)
 INSERT INTO _ibis_tmp_table_insert_efv33lul9euv9qwo963bop9rm (id, a) SELECT t1.id, t0.a 
FROM dg_test AS t1 JOIN t0 ON t1.id = t0.id
```

### What version of ibis are you using?

6.0.0

### What backend(s) are you using, if any?

Postgres

issue.title: CTE Compiles in Incorrect Order for Postgres Insert From Select

labels.name: external driver issues
labels.description: the issue involves a misbehavior on the part of the DBAPI itself, probably not SQLAlchemy

labels.name: expected behavior
labels.description: that's how it's meant to work.  consider the "documentation" label in addition

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

The issue described [here](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4275) for the Oracle engine and fixed [here](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/3619edcb8aa3ceef2a44925b85315fc0e90c5982) for the Oracle engine and MySQL engine also exists for the Postgres engine. I have used the same code example from this previous issue to reproduce the error.

When attempting to execute an SQL statement with a common table expression insert using a Postgres engine, the insert statements render with a syntax error. The `insert into` statement should be at the beginning of the query, but instead is in the middle.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

1.4.46

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg2

### Database Vendor and Major Version

Redshift 1.0.5

### Python Version

3.9

### Operating system

Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Table, Column, Integer, select, MetaData, String

engine = create_engine('postgresql://username:password@host:port/database')

metadata = MetaData()

foo = Table('foo', metadata, Column('name', String(1)), schema='test_schema')
baz = Table(
    'baz',
    metadata,
    Column('id', Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=False),
    Column('name', String(50)),
    schema='test_schema'
)


metadata.create_all(engine)

cte_1 = select([foo.c.name]).cte('first_cte')
cte_2 = select([cte_1.c.name]).select_from(cte_1).cte('second_cte')
ins = baz.insert().from_select([baz.c.name], cte_2)

print(ins.compile(engine))

with engine.begin() as conn:
    conn.execute(ins)
```


### Error

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sqlalchemy_mvc.py", line 26, in <module>
    conn.execute(ins)
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1380, in execute
    return meth(self, multiparams, params, _EMPTY_EXECUTION_OPTS)
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py", line 334, in _execute_on_connection
    return connection._execute_clauseelement(
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1572, in _execute_clauseelement
    ret = self._execute_context(
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1943, in _execute_context
    self._handle_dbapi_exception(
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 2124, in _handle_dbapi_exception
    util.raise_(
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/compat.py", line 211, in raise_
    raise exception
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1900, in _execute_context
    self.dialect.do_execute(
  File "/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/default.py", line 736, in do_execute
    cursor.execute(statement, parameters)
sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.errors.SyntaxError) syntax error at or near "INSERT"
LINE 7:  INSERT INTO test_schema.baz (name) SELECT second_cte.nam...
         ^

[SQL: WITH first_cte AS 
(SELECT test_schem.foo.name AS name 
FROM test_schema.foo), 
second_cte AS 
(SELECT first_cte.name AS name 
FROM first_cte)
 INSERT INTO test_schema.baz (name) SELECT second_cte.name 
FROM second_cte]
(Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/14/f405)
```

### Additional context

I was able to resolve the issue after forking the package with [this](https://github.com/110holmberg/sqlalchemy/commit/865a4b60da8a40b6cd339855998edc9b6e90ce79) one line change that takes advantage of the original fix that was implemented for Oracle and MySQL in [this](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/3619edcb8aa3ceef2a44925b85315fc0e90c5982) PR.
